name_ru: Да И Цзя Цзи То Ча
aliases: Menghai Da Yi Jia Ji Tuo
processing: A factory blend of sun-dried raw large-leaf tea steamed and pressed into a bowl-shaped tuo, without a ripening pile.
harvest_season: Blended from stock, so no single picking is claimed; the production year is printed on the wrapper.
appearance_dry: A compact dark green nest of tightly pressed leaf.
appearance_liquor: Golden yellow in young tuos, deepening with age.
appearance_wet: Mixed chopped and whole large-leaf pieces, yellow-green to olive.
taste_profile: Sold as a thick, strong Menghai blend. As with other young factory raw tuos, expect firm bitterness and astringency that round out with storage.

brewing.notes: Break the tuo gently with a pick and let it rest a little before brewing; tight pressing makes the first steeps uneven.

vintage_note: Sold by production year, with the batch printed on the packaging, and factory releases are bought both to drink young and to store. As with other Menghai raw blends, expect the tea to soften over 5 to 10 years or more with sensible storage. Prices depend on the year and on whether the wrapper is genuine.
description:
Jiaji Tuocha is a raw pu-erh tuo from the Menghai Tea Factory under its Dayi brand. Jiaji means 'grade A', and the tea sits among the factory's pressed bowls as a higher-grade blended product.

It is a blend, so its point is consistency instead of a single place or tree. Pressing it into a tuo makes a dense, slow-opening tea, and the small size makes it an easy way into factory raw pu-erh.

Expect the thick, heavy Menghai character that sellers describe. As with other young factory raw teas it can be bitter when new, and shorter steeps help. Some storage helps more.

Buy from a seller who handles Dayi regularly and check the batch details on the wrapper. The exact recipe is not public, and the name alone tells you little about any given year.
history: The Menghai Tea Factory was founded in 1940, and its Dayi trademark came into use decades later. Little is documented about when the Jiaji tuo first appeared or how its blend has changed, and the factory does not publish the recipe.
